lines.trans: Been drinking yesterday?
Is it noticeable?
Your face is pale, your hands are shaking a bit.
Yes, the night was very wild.
Enjoy your meal.
Who did you just say that to?
To a guest at the next table.
Would you like anything?
Water.
Sparkling or still?
A liter! Without any gas at all!
Right away, I am already bringing it.
Thank you, my friend, you are saving my life.

Is it noticeable?
Would you like anything?
Water.
A liter! Without any gas at all!
Been drinking yesterday?
Is it noticeable?
Your face is pale, your hands are shaking a bit.
Yes, the night was very wild.
Enjoy your meal.
Who did you just say that to?
To a guest at the next table.
Would you like anything?
Water.
Sparkling or still?
A liter! Without any gas at all!
Right away, I am already bringing it.
Thank you, my friend, you are saving my life.
Cold water is the best medicine.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'appetite', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('!') (= Enjoy your meal!) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Russian preposition meaning 'without' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Qualitative or relational adjective formed with the productive '-н-' suffix, meaning 'pale' and agreeing in gender, number, and case.

examples.text: У него сегодня очень бледное лицо.
examples.trans: He has a very pale face today.
Your face is pale, your hands are shaking a bit.

examples.text: Ты выглядишь очень бледным и страшно испуганным.
examples.trans: You look very pale and terribly frightened.

meanings.note: Qualitative or relational adjective formed with the productive '-н-' suffix, meaning 'wild' and agreeing in gender, number, and case.

examples.text: У них была бурная ночь в клубе.
examples.trans: They had a wild night at the club.
Yes, the night was very wild.

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to booze', forming an aspectual pair with 'набухаться'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Ты слишком много бухал вчера ночью.
examples.trans: You drank too much booze last night.

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Secondary conversational sense ('there is, there are') (present есть; у меня есть = I have) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('all') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.
Secondary conversational sense ('everything') (neuter всё) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('everyone') (plural все) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Common feminine noun meaning 'water' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Vanya, the water! There's water everywhere!

всякий.gloss: every kind of, all sorts of, any

meanings.en: all sorts of, every kind of
meanings.note: всякое бывает = all sorts of things happen
Secondary conversational sense ('any, every') (на всякий случай = just in case) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Alright, all sorts of things happen.
Take an umbrella just in case.

examples.text: Ладно, всякое бывает. Ну что вы?
examples.trans: Alright, all sorts of things happen. Oh, come on.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'yesterday'.

examples.text: Я вчера ел маринованные грибы. Может, один гриб был плохой.
examples.trans: Yesterday I ate pickled mushrooms. Maybe one mushroom was bad.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'gas', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Я пью минеральную воду без газа.
examples.trans: I drink mineral water without gas.
A liter! Without any gas at all!

meanings.note: Abstract masculine noun formed with the productive Slavic suffix '-ость', denoting the quality or state of 'guest'.

examples.trans: All the guests love them very much.

examples.text: Сегодня вечером к нам придут гости.
examples.trans: Guests are coming to our place tonight.

meanings.note: emphatic at the start of a sentence
Secondary conversational sense ('? = really?, oh yeah?') (disbelief) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to tremble', forming an aspectual pair with 'задрожать'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Его руки немного дрожат от усталости.
examples.trans: His hands are shaking a bit from exhaustion.
Your face is pale, your hands are shaking a bit.
Why are you trembling so much?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'friend' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: This is Vanya, my childhood friend.

examples.text: Это Паша, мой заместитель. Это Ваня, друг моего детства.
examples.trans: This is Pasha, my deputy. This is Vanya, my childhood friend.

meanings.note: + dative of person + genitive of thing: желаю вам удачи

examples.trans: Good health to you, sir! (I wish you health!)

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'life' in everyday Russian.
Russian preposition meaning 'for' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('behind') (+ instrumental) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'noticeably'.

examples.text: Его волнение было заметно каждому человеку.
examples.trans: His nervousness was noticeable to everyone.

examples.text: Скажи честно, царапину на бампере очень сильно заметно?
examples.trans: Tell me honestly, is the scratch on the bumper very noticeable?

examples.text: После похвалы шефа настроение на кухне заметно улучшилось.
examples.trans: After the chef's praise, the mood in the kitchen noticeably improved.

meanings.note: Coordinating or subordinating Russian conjunction meaning 'or', linking clauses in spoken dialogue.
in the instrumental: 'кем ты работаешь?'

examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, who are your rivals?

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'medicine, medication' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The doctor prescribed a new medicine.

examples.text: Может быть, лекарства какие-то? Лекарства вам нужны?
examples.trans: Maybe some medicine? Do you need medicine?

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'liter', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Официант принёс целый литр чистой воды.
examples.trans: The waiter brought a whole liter of clean water.
A liter! Without any gas at all!
Five liters of cognac every week.

meanings.note: Declinable neuter noun meaning 'face', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('person, individual') (formal) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: He has a very kind face.

examples.text: Карамельно-сливочный цвет. Очень тебе к лицу! Надень куртку.
examples.trans: A caramel-cream colour. It really suits you! Put the jacket on.

meanings.note: лучший в мире = the best in the world
Secondary conversational sense ('better') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Ты мне даёшь пятьсот рублей, а я выхожу и покупаю тебе лучшую приставку в мире.
examples.trans: You give me five hundred roubles, and I get out and buy you the best console in the world.

meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'много'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: I need to do a bit of work.

examples.text: Мы даём вам ещё немного времени.
examples.trans: We are giving you a little more time.

meanings.note: one direction, now; 'Неси!' = Bring (it)!

examples.trans: Yulia, bring a pen and a piece of paper.

meanings.note: ночью = at night; спокойной ночи = good night

examples.text: Ну что, Аркаша? Наступила ночь, просыпается мафия.
examples.trans: So, Arkasha? Night has fallen, the mafia wakes up.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'very'.
Secondary conversational sense ('very much') (with verbs: очень люблю) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Qualitative or relational adjective formed with the productive '-н-' suffix, meaning 'pleasant' and agreeing in gender, number, and case.
Secondary conversational sense ('!') (= Enjoy your meal!) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Very well! Have a pleasant evening.

meanings.note: Derived feminine noun formed with a productive Slavic suffix, used in spoken Russian to mean 'hand'.
+ instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: 'сейчас буду' = I'll be right there
Secondary conversational sense ('in a moment') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: once; что скажешь? = what do you say?
Secondary conversational sense ('tell me / tell us') (polite request) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Tell us, when will your programme be out?

meanings.note: Qualitative or relational adjective formed with the productive '-н-' suffix, meaning 'neighboring' and agreeing in gender, number, and case.

examples.text: За соседним столиком сидели приятные люди.
examples.trans: Pleasant people were sitting at the next table.
To a guest at the next table.

examples.text: В соседнем зале играет тихая музыка.
examples.trans: Quiet music plays in the neighboring hall.

meanings.en: to save, to rescue from danger
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'пасать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to save, to rescue', paired with 'спасти'.

examples.text: Все прибежали тебя спасать — и я, и папа!
examples.trans: Everyone came running to save you — both me and Dad!
She is saving you from the hospital!

meanings.note: спасибо за + accusative = thank you for

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Derived masculine noun formed with a productive Slavic suffix, used in spoken Russian to mean 'small table'.

examples.text: Они заняли свободный столик у окна.
examples.trans: They took a free table near the window.
Would you like to sit at an available table?
To a guest at the next table.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('you') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: уже четыре года = for four years now

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been mayor for four years now.

meanings.note: Qualitative or relational adjective formed with the productive '-н-' suffix, meaning 'cold' and agreeing in gender, number, and case.
Secondary conversational sense ('unfriendly, cold') (emotion) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: You are a good woman. Cold.

examples.text: Эта тарелка уже совсем холодная, её нельзя подавать гостю!
examples.trans: This plate is already completely cold, it cannot be served to a guest!

meanings.note: any thing at all, not a particular one

examples.text: Правда, Нин, всё нормально. Скажи что-нибудь, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: Honestly, Nina, everything's fine. Say something, please.
Are you doing anything about it?

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine
Secondary conversational sense ('is') (linking word: главное — это народ) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
